legs.result: The targeted replica's FROMLEADER update reached the servlet filter (arrival latch); the real stall detector reported a nonempty queue (60 remaining elements) and the SolrCmdDistributor error hook observed that error before the update completed; the replica then showed leader-ineligible in the shard terms, entered RECOVERING while the recovery pause was held, and after the pause was released became ACTIVE and leader-eligible again. Real-time-get reads with distrib=false on the specific leader and the specific target replica compared all 64 acknowledged documents and every _version_ matched. No precondition failed or was skipped at either seed; no flakiness or non-reproduction observed across the two runs.

The injection is deterministic in shape: the filter never reads the request, the 64-document batch (16 fields of 8KB per document) blocks the streaming writer on backpressure, later updates stay queued, and the detector fires at its 1000ms threshold (observed 1250ms). The recovery pause is held by the test until after the leader has processed the error and changed the terms, so the RECOVERING observation is the pause's doing, not a race; the stalled request's own 90-second filter timeout never stands in for the stall (detection at about 1.25s, update completion asserted separately). Errors are not masked: the hook asserts the exact stall message content, and teardown clears the hook, the filter control and the pause.
